clue.text: Movie queen from the continent

definitions.meaning: the film The ... Queen, a 1951 Bogart and Hepburn classic, so its queen carries this word
belonging to or coming from Africa

explanation.surface: A film star of royal status hails from a far-off land.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Movie queen' is a cryptic pointer to the title 'The African Queen'; the queen in that film is described by the word needed.
explanation.definitionFit: The adjective describes anything native to or originating in Africa, the continent.

clue.text: A rise for flying men, now well off

indicators.note: in a down clue a rising word reads from bottom to top, so the letters go backwards

parts.note: the RAF, the Royal Air Force, is a body of flying men

explanation.surface: An RAF promotion has left the airmen comfortably rich.
explanation.walkthrough: 'well off' looks like 'wealthy' but means a good distance away; in a down clue 'rise' reads the airmen upwards.
explanation.definitionFit: Far away and well off both describe something at a great distance.

clue.text: Fled before the start of the storm

indicators.note: one piece is placed before the next in the answer

parts.note: fled means ran away, past tense of run

indicators.note: the opening letter of the following word is wanted

explanation.surface: Someone bolted just as the tempest began.
explanation.walkthrough: The T is the start of 'the', not of 'storm', which is the definition, used as a verb meaning to rage noisily.
explanation.definitionFit: To storm is to shout and rage angrily, which is to rave or harangue.

clue.text: One abandoned by actors on tour

parts.note: the actors in a play make up its cast
a touring team or company is away from home

explanation.surface: A performer is left behind by the rest of the company travelling.
explanation.definitionFit: A person marooned or deserted, typically on an island, is a shipwrecked outcast.

clue.text: Scot gets lift with sailors on the Moray Firth

indicators.note: in a down clue lifting a word turns it upward, reading backwards

parts.note: Ian is a typically Scottish first name
RN, the Royal Navy, stands for sailors

explanation.surface: A Scotsman hitches a ride with navy men along the Scottish coast.
explanation.walkthrough: NAIRN is a Scottish town on the Moray Firth, an inlet on Scotland's north-east coast; the definition describes the place by its location.
explanation.definitionFit: This Highland town sits on the southern shore of that northern Scottish estuary, so it is a place located there.

clue.text: Chest is tender after cold

indicators.note: the second piece follows the first

parts.note: C is the abbreviation for cold, as on a tap
to tender is to offer, as in tendering a bid

explanation.surface: A sore chest that follows a chill.
explanation.walkthrough: 'tender' reads as sore, but here it is the verb meaning to put forward.
explanation.definitionFit: A strongbox or treasure chest for keeping money or valuables.

clue.text: Choose not to be involved with pot?

parts.note: reading the instruction as wordplay, OPT is the word pot with its letters out of order, so it is 'pot' put out

explanation.surface: Someone declines to join in with the cannabis smoking.
explanation.walkthrough: Read the answer as an instruction: rearrange ('out') the letters of OPT and you get pot, so the clue's 'pot?' is what the answer describes.
explanation.definitionFit: To withdraw from a scheme or arrangement by choice is a phrasal verb of declining.

clue.text: A course in aviation

parts.note: reads like a training programme for pilots, but means the route an aircraft follows

explanation.definitionFit: The planned track through the sky that an aircraft follows is its route in the air.

clue.text: Car and lorry close after crash

indicators.note: the letters are wrecked as if in a collision and reassembled

explanation.surface: A motor and a truck come together after an accident.
explanation.definitionFit: A luxury British motorcar brand, so a car of that make.

clue.text: Acting so strangely when in doubt

indicators.note: letters arranged in an odd way are reordered

explanation.surface: Someone behaves oddly whenever they are unsure.
explanation.definitionFit: An agnostic holds that nothing can be known for certain about God, so is doubtful.

clue.text: When one chooses, return thanks to Shakespeare

indicators.note: returning a word means reading it backwards

parts.note: ta is British informal for thanks
William Shakespeare is often called Will

explanation.surface: Send thanks back to the Bard whenever you like.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom means as and when a person wishes, freely by choice.

clue.text: I breathe fresh air in the peninsula

parts.note: to breathe is to live, to exist, to be

indicators.note: fresh means new, so the letters get a new arrangement

explanation.surface: A traveller enjoys clean air on a coastal promontory.
explanation.walkthrough: 'breathe' stands for simply existing, a loose but fair equivalent of 'be'; 'fresh' is the anagram signal for the last word.
explanation.definitionFit: The landmass holding Spain and Portugal is a large south-west European peninsula.

clue.text: What had P. Rubens at his disposal?

definitions.text: What had P. Rubens at his disposal?

indicators.note: the letters are disposed, or set out, in a new order

explanation.surface: Asking what tools the Flemish painter Rubens had to hand.
explanation.walkthrough: The whole clue defines and builds: rearrange P RUBENS AT HIS, signalled by 'disposal', for the tools a painter has.
explanation.definitionFit: A painter like Rubens would have brushes for applying paint at hand.

clue.text: As a rule, it lacks civility

definitions.text: As a rule, it lacks civility

parts.words: As a rule, it lacks civility
parts.note: reads as a remark on manners, but describes rule by the army in place of civil government

explanation.definitionFit: Military government imposed in place of civilian authority, so a regime without civil rule.

clue.text: She provides flying courses

parts.note: suggests a flight instructor, but means a woman serving meal courses aboard an aircraft

explanation.definitionFit: A female cabin attendant serves passengers food on airliners.

clue.text: Picture house

parts.note: looks like an old name for a cinema, but means a building where paintings are shown

explanation.definitionFit: A gallery exhibiting paintings is literally a house for pictures.

clue.text: Editorial boss

definitions.meaning: a newspaper's main opinion article, a leading article
the person in charge, the head

explanation.definitionFit: Both a newspaper's opinion column and a chief or head go by this word.

clue.text: One in favour of being paid?

definitions.meaning: a professional is paid, unlike an amateur

explanation.definitionFit: The word means both an argument or person for something and short for professional.

clue.text: An air of simplicity appropriate for a sailor's accessories?

definitions.text: An air of simplicity appropriate for a sailor's accessories?

parts.words: An air of simplicity appropriate for a sailor's accessories?
parts.note: a simple air is a little song, and a sailor's holdall for odds and ends shares that name

explanation.definitionFit: Sailors kept sewing kit and small personal items in a small cloth sack of that name.

clue.text: Pull away from the east

definitions.meaning: to haul or drag something along behind
heading ..., that is to the west, away from the east

explanation.definitionFit: To haul a vehicle behind is to drag it; split as TO W it means westwards.

clue.text: Not believing a lot can be changed

definitions.text: Not believing a lot can be changed

parts.words: Not believing a lot can be changed
parts.note: lot here means one's fate, which such a person thinks is fixed

explanation.definitionFit: Someone resigned to fate believes events are predetermined and unalterable.

clue.text: Extension of a letter, say

indicators.note: say signals that the words are spoken and heard

parts.note: a letter of the alphabet, X, said as 'an ex'

explanation.surface: A postscript adds length to a letter.
explanation.walkthrough: 'a letter' is an X, and 'an ex' said aloud sounds like the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: A building added to a main one is an extension.

clue.text: Plans to give scope to people in the arts

indicators.note: one piece is placed inside the word arts

parts.note: taken as written
range means scope or extent
men stands for people

explanation.surface: Proposals to widen opportunities for creative types.
explanation.definitionFit: Preparations or plans are things arranged beforehand.

clue.text: We hear forty of the Romans do better

indicators.note: signals that the letters are said aloud

parts.note: XL is forty in Roman numerals

explanation.surface: Rumour has it forty Roman soldiers performed better.
explanation.definitionFit: To excel is to outdo others, to surpass them.

clue.text: Is unable to lean over

explanation.definitionFit: The contraction of cannot means unable; to tilt to one side is also this word.

clue.text: Find love on the German river

indicators.note: in a down clue one piece sits on top of the next

parts.note: love is zero in tennis, O
der is a German word for the

explanation.surface: Romance found on a riverbank in Germany.
explanation.definitionFit: The Oder is a river forming much of the German-Polish border.

clue.text: Made eyes flushed, although on the sheltered side

parts.note: the lee is the side sheltered from the wind
a flushed face is red

explanation.surface: Someone ogled with a blush while standing out of the wind.
explanation.definitionFit: To leer is to look at someone suggestively, so to make eyes at them.

clue.text: One who didn't strike Shakespeare as a sword carrier

parts.note: a scab is a worker who refuses to join a strike
Shakespeare is known as the Bard

explanation.surface: A strikebreaker regarded by the playwright as an armed man.
explanation.definitionFit: A sheath for a sword holds the blade when not in use.

clue.text: His cricket records still stand today

definitions.text: His cricket records still stand today

parts.words: His cricket records still stand today
parts.note: sounds like a great batsman's achievements, but means the publisher whose annual almanack records cricket

explanation.walkthrough: John Wisden founded the Cricketers' Almanack, the annual book of cricket records, still published.
explanation.definitionFit: The almanack bearing this founder's name is cricket's standard yearly book of records.

clue.text: Open boat in spill

definitions.meaning: a flat-bottomed barge for unloading ships
a spill is a thin strip of wood or paper for lighting fires

explanation.definitionFit: A barge used to ferry cargo shares its name with a thing that kindles a flame, like a spill.
